---
title: "Code"
subtitle: "Inline code and fenced blocks"
---

Inline code uses IBM Plex Mono on the highlight token. Fenced blocks use a
transparent fill within a 1px frame with a 5px radius. Padding keeps the copy
control clear of the first line.

Filename blocks add a softly tinted header inside the same frame. Quarto
supplies the source and the `code-copy` availability setting; Askr uses its
shared text `Copy` button instead of Quarto's icon-and-tooltip control.

After a successful copy, the button shows `Copied!` with a green outline for
about two seconds, then returns to `Copy`. Long lines in scroll-enabled blocks
stay inside the block instead of widening the page.

An inline sample is `askr-html`.

```python
def describe_reading_surface(theme: str, width: int) -> str:
    return f"{theme} surface at {width}px retains local overflow boundaries"

long_line = "qdk keeps this intentionally long source line in a local preformatted scroll area rather than allowing it to widen the whole page beyond the reader viewport"
print(describe_reading_surface("dark", 360), long_line)
```

```{.python filename="reading.py"}
def quiet(width: int) -> str:
    return f"measure {width}px"
```

## Filename inside a callout

A native filename labels the block without adding another card. Long paths
scroll within the code area; the filename can wrap on a narrow screen.

::: {.callout-note title="Example output paths" collapse="false"}
These generic paths illustrate a report manifest, not a live filesystem.

```{.default filename="reports/example-run/output-manifest.txt" .code-overflow-scroll}
layout: /work/projects/example-study/runs/reference-model/exports/geometry/component-layout.svg
results: /work/projects/example-study/runs/reference-model/analysis/frequency-sweep/results.csv
report: /work/projects/example-study/runs/reference-model/reports/summary/index.html
```
:::

## Limits

The filename example keeps a long source line inside its scrollable block.
Do not wrap a paragraph in a code fence to force a measure; prose belongs in
the article, and a fence is for source.
